rule: cell k = trunc(bearing / 11.25); cell k shows heading 11.25k. One row: the tube never tilts up or down.
note: The original Flash Cannon (top.3.png, one picture for all ten levels) in 3D, from cannonflash3d.py. pivot = middle of each cell (the tube's turning point, in its collar on the drum's top); heading = ground bearing in degrees (0 down-right on screen, 45 at the viewer). The body's parts in front of the tube are cut out of each cell, so no front layer is needed. The tube leans barrel_tilt_deg off upright toward its heading, always: the shot starts at `muzzle` (the middle of the tube's mouth) and the game works out the lob.
heights_note: muzzle_height_px: the mouth above the ground, game px measured like a ground distance (same at every heading); muzzle_height_screen_px: the same seen on screen; ground_below_pivot_px: screen px from the pivot down to the ground under it.
aim_note: aim_deg: on-screen direction the barrel points (0 = right, 90 = down), measured from the 3D model; muzzle: [dx, dy] game px from the pivot to the muzzle tip on screen; ground_deg: on-screen direction of the cell's heading on the ground; aim_len: barrel length on screen in game px (short = pointing at or away from the viewer).
